extracted.intended_audience: users of the PARI/GP library (computational number theorists and developers working with relative number field/rnf routines)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP routines dealing with relative number fields (rnf*, rnf- prefixed functions) and related algebraic-number utilities, describing required inputs, outputs, flags, and important caveats.

rubrics_metrics.name: polredbest flag=1 output form
rubrics_metrics.description: If flag = 1: outputs a two-component row vector [P, a], where P is the default output and Mod(a, P) is a root of the original T.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: [P,a] = polredbest(x^4 + 8, 1) returns [x^4 + 2, Mod(x^3, x^4 + 2)]; the map Q[x]/(T) -> Q[x]/(P), x -> Mod(a,P) defines an isomorphism which can be computed with subst(lift(Q),'x,a).

rubrics_metrics.name: polredord obsolete
rubrics_metrics.description: polredord(x) is obsolete; use polredbest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN polredord(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: poltschirnhaus transformation usage
rubrics_metrics.description: poltschirnhaus(x) applies a random Tschirnhausen transformation to polynomial x (assumed non-constant and separable) to obtain a new equation for the étale algebra defined by x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when computing resolvents; used by polgalois. Library syntax GEN tschirnhaus(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfalgtobasis: input & effect
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfalgtobasis(rnf, x) expresses x on the relative integral basis. rnf is a relative number field extension L/K (output by rnfinit), and x is an element of L in absolute form (polynomial or polmod with polmod coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfalgtobasis(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfbasis: allowed inputs and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfbasis(bnf, M) — M is a projective ZK-module of rank n given by a pseudo-basis of size n; the routine returns either a true ZK-basis of M (size n) if it exists, or an n+1-element generating set if not. It is allowed to use an irreducible polynomial P in K[X] instead of M, in which case M is defined as the ring of integers of K[X]/(P) viewed as a ZK-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfbasis(GEN bnf, GEN M).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfbasistoalg: conversion to polmod form
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfbasistoalg(rnf, x) computes representation of x as a polmod with polmods coefficients; rnf is rnfinit output and x is expressed on the relative integral basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfbasistoalg(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfcharpoly: characteristic polynomial in nf[X]/(T)
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfcharpoly(nf, T, a, {var = x}) returns the characteristic polynomial of a over nf, where a belongs to nf[X]/(T). Returns a polynomial in variable var (x by default).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: rnfcharpoly(nf, x^2+y*x+1, x+y) returns x^2 + Mod(-y, y^2+1)*x + 1. Library syntax GEN rnfcharpoly(GEN nf, GEN T, GEN a, long var = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfconductor output format
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfconductor(bnf, pol) computes the class field theory conductor of an Abelian relative polynomial pol; returns a 3-component vector [conductor, bnr, subgroup].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: conductor is [f0, f∞], bnr is attached bnr structure, subgroup is HNF matrix defining subgroup of ray class group. Library syntax GEN rnfconductor(GEN bnf, GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdedekind behavior & flags
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfdedekind(nf, pol, {pr}, {flag = 0}) applies Dedekind's criterion to the order ZK[X]/(P) at prime ideal pr. pr may be vector of primes or omitted (then maximality at all primes is tested and flag auto=1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default behavior (flag 0 or omitted and single pr): returns [max, basis, v] where basis = pseudo-basis of enlarged order O, max = 1 if O proven pr-maximal else 0, v = valuation at pr of order discriminant. If flag non-zero return 1 if order is pr-maximal (or maximal at all relevant primes) and 0 otherwise (much faster). Use rnfpseudobasis for more information; routine may fail in some projective-line residue cases. Library syntax GEN rnfdedekind(GEN nf, GEN pol, GEN pr = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdet: determinant of pseudo-matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfdet(nf, M) computes determinant of pseudo-matrix M over maximal order of nf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfdet(GEN nf, GEN M).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfdisc output format & variable priority
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfdisc(nf, pol) computes relative discriminant of L over K and returns [D, d] where D is relative ideal discriminant and d is discriminant as element of nf*/nf*2. The main variable of nf must be of lower priority than that of pol.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfdiscf(GEN nf, GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltabstorel: input forms and initialization requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfeltabstorel(rnf, x) takes x expressed as polynomial modulo absolute equation rnf.pol or in terms of absolute Z-basis and computes x as element of relative extension L/K as polmod with polmod coefficients. If ZL not initialized, nfinit(rnf) must be called first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show errors if rnf not initialized; initialize with nfinit(rnf). Library syntax GEN rnfeltabstorel(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltdown: downwards conversion and flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfeltdown(rnf, x, {flag = 0}) computes x (element of L) as element of K as a t_POLMOD if flag = 0 and as a t_COL otherwise; if x not in K, a domain error occurs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires absolute nf structure for certain inputs; examples show type errors if improper types are given. Library syntax GEN rnfeltdown0(GEN rnf, GEN x, long flag) or GEN rnfeltdown(GEN rnf, GEN x) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltnorm: relative norm
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfeltnorm(rnf, x) returns the relative norm N_{L/K}(x) as an element of K; rnf is rnfinit output and x an element of L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show rnfeltnorm(L, Mod(x,L.pol)) etc. Library syntax GEN rnfeltnorm(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltreltoabs: relative-to-absolute conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfeltreltoabs(rnf, x) computes x (element of L given with polmod with polmod coefficients) as element of absolute extension L/Q as polynomial modulo rnf.pol (absolute equation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate conversions of Mod(x, L.pol) etc. Library syntax GEN rnfeltreltoabs(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfelttrace: relative trace
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfelttrace(rnf, x) returns the relative trace Tr_{L/K}(x) as an element of K.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: trace of Mod(x,L.pol) is 0, of 2 is 4 etc. Library syntax GEN rnfelttrace(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfeltup: up-conversion and flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfeltup(rnf, x, {flag = 0}) computes x (element of K) as an element of absolute extension L/Q as a t_POLMOD modulo rnf.pol if flag = 0 and as t_COL on absolute field integer basis if flag = 1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relative structure lacks absolute nf, certain calls fail; examples show nfinit(L) adds absolute nf structure. Library syntax GEN rnfeltup0(GEN rnf, GEN x, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfequation: absolute equation computation and flag output
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfequation(nf, pol, {flag = 0}) computes an absolute equation of L over Q given relative polynomial pol over nf. Main variable of nf must have lower priority than pol. If pol reducible but squarefree, the result is absolute equation of the étale algebra defined by pol. If pol not squarefree, raises DOMAIN exception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag non-zero, outputs [z, a, k] where z is absolute equation, a is t_POLMOD modulo z giving root α of base-field polynomial, k small integer s.t. θ = β + kα is root of z. Examples and suggested workflow for handling k ≠ 0 are provided. Library syntax GEN rnfequation0(GEN nf, GEN pol, long flag) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfhnfbasis: HNF bnf-basis existence
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfhnfbasis(bnf, x) returns a true bnf-basis of L in upper triangular Hermite normal form if it exists, and returns 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input x either polynomial with coefficients in bnf or pseudo-basis. Library syntax GEN rnfhnfbasis(GEN bnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealabstorel: converting absolute ideal to relative
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealabstorel(rnf, x) takes an ideal x of the absolute extension L/Q given by a Z-basis of elements of L and returns the relative pseudo-matrix in HNF giving x considered as ZK-module (relative ideal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you already have an absolute nf Labs and m in HNF for L, then pass Labs.zk * m to convert m to a relative ideal. Examples and library syntax GEN rnfidealabstorel(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealdown: compute ideal below
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealdown(rnf, x) returns the ideal of K below x (intersection of x with K).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input x an ideal of L given in relative form or by Z-basis; library syntax GEN rnfidealdown(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealfactor: factoring ideals in L
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealfactor(rnf, x) factors the ideal x into prime ideal powers in the attached absolute number field L = nfinit(rnf). Output format similar to factor; prime ideals represented as by idealprimedec for L.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: ideals of base field K must be explicitly lifted to L via rnfidealup before factoring. Library syntax GEN rnfidealfactor(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealhnf: compute HNF pseudo-matrix for relative ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealhnf(rnf, x) computes the HNF pseudo-matrix attached to x viewed as ZK-module; x may be many types (elements, matrices, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfidealhnf(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealmul: relative ideal multiplication
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealmul(rnf, x, y) given two ideals x,y of relative extension L/K (as pseudo-matrices), outputs ideal product as relative ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfidealmul(GEN rnf, GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealnormabs: absolute norm of relative ideal (fast)
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealnormabs(rnf, x) computes the norm of x considered as an ideal of absolute extension L/Q. It is identical to idealnorm(rnf, rnfidealnormrel(rnf,x)) but faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfidealnormabs(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealnormrel: relative ideal norm
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealnormrel(rnf, x) computes the relative norm of x as an ideal of K in HNF.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfidealnormrel(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealprimedec: prime decomposition above a prime
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealprimedec(rnf, pr) completes rnf with an nf structure attached to L and returns the prime ideal decomposition of pr in L/K. pr may be a maximal ideal (prid) or a prime number p; in latter case returns [SK, SL] where SK contains primes of K above p and SL[i] is vector of primes of L above SK[i].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completing rnf may be performed implicitly. Library syntax GEN rnfidealprimedec(GEN rnf, GEN pr).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealreltoabs: conversion and flag tradeoff
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealreltoabs(rnf, x, {flag = 0}) returns the relative ideal x as an absolute ideal of L/Q. If flag=0 returns vector of t_POLMODs modulo rnf.pol forming Z-basis; if flag=1 returns HNF in terms of fixed Z-basis for ZL but will complete rnf (expensive) if needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default avoids completing rnf to reduce cost when absolute degree is large. Library syntax GEN rnfidealreltoabs0(GEN rnf, GEN x, long flag) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealtwoelt: provide two generators of ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealtwoelt(rnf, x) given a relative ideal x (pseudo-matrix) returns a vector of two generators of x over ZL expressed as polmods with polmod coefficients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfidealtwoelement(GEN rnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfidealup: lifting base-field ideal to L and flag semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfidealup(rnf, x, {flag = 0}) returns the ideal xZ_L as an absolute ideal of L/Q in the form of a Z-basis. If flag=0 result given by vector of polynomials modulo rnf.pol; if flag=1 result given in HNF in terms of fixed Z-basis for ZL (completes rnf, expensive).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default avoids completing rnf for efficiency. Library syntax GEN rnfidealup0(GEN rnf, GEN x, long flag) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfinit: construction semantics, flag effects, and field layout
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfinit(nf, pol, {flag = 0}) computes data to work in relative extension L/K defined by pol over nf. The main variable of pol must have higher priority than that of nf; coefficients of pol must be in nf. Result is a row vector with many technical fields; if flag=1, add an nf structure attached to L (expensive) which fixes integer basis for ZL and allows absolute forms for elements and ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed descriptions of rnf fields rnf[1]..rnf[12] are provided: pol (relative polynomial), integer basis for K as elements of L, rnf.disc, rnf.index, rnf.zk (pseudo-basis for ZL as ZK-module), inverse matrix, rnf.nf (nf), an extension vector [P,a,k,K.pol,pol] describing absolute extension, and an optional storage field. Caveat: if k != 0 absolute and relative generators differ — suggested workflow given to substitute pol accordingly. Library syntax GEN rnfinit0(GEN nf, GEN pol, long flag) and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisabelian: abelian extension test
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfisabelian(nf, T) returns 1 if T (relative polynomial) defines an abelian extension, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax long rnfisabelian(GEN nf, GEN T).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisfree: freeness test for ZK-module
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfisfree(bnf, x) given bnf from bnfinit and polynomial or pseudo-basis x returns 1 if L/bnf is free, 0 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax long rnfisfree(GEN bnf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfislocalcyclo: local cyclotomic test for p-power degree
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfislocalcyclo(rnf) (when [L:K] is a power of a prime p) returns 1 if the p-extension is locally cyclotomic (contained locally in cyclotomic Z_p-extension at all v|p), and 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate expected behavior and continuity by Krasner's lemma. Library syntax long rnfislocalcyclo(GEN rnf).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisnorm: solving relative norm equations and guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfisnorm(T, a, {flag = 0}) attempts to decide whether a in K is a norm from L/K using precomputed data T from rnfisnorminit. Output is [x, q] where a = Norm(x) * q, searching for x an S-integer where S contains at least ramified primes, class group generators, and primes dividing a. If L/K is Galois the answer is guaranteed (q=1 iff a is a norm); otherwise, under GRH it's guaranteed if S contains all primes less than 12 log2 |disc(M)| where M is normal closure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rnfisnorminit determined L/K Galois and flag=0, a Warning is issued so user can set flag=1 to check Galois-ness according to T. Library syntax GEN rnfisnorm(GEN T, GEN a, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfisnorminit: precomputation flags
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfisnorminit(pol, polrel, {flag = 2}) computes technical data needed by rnfisnorm. If flag = 0 do not care whether L/K is Galois; if flag = 1 assume L/K is Galois (unchecked) which speeds up rnfisnorm; if flag = 2 let routine determine whether L/K is Galois.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfisnorminit(GEN pol, GEN polrel, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfkummer: Kummer-based class field equations and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfkummer(bnr, {subgp}, {d = 0}) finds a relative equation for class field corresponding to module in bnr and congruence subgroup; if d>0 outputs all relative equations of degree d contained in ray class field with same conductor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: only works for subgroups of prime index; uses Kummer theory and adjoins roots of unity (requires a costly bnfinit), finds generator via Hecke's characterization. For non-prime degree extensions, user must split extension manually as tower/compositum of prime-degree extensions. Library syntax GEN rnfkummer(GEN bnr, GEN subgp = NULL, long d, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnflllgram: order reduction via LLL/Gram
rubrics_metrics.description: rnflllgram(nf, pol, order) given relative polynomial and a suborder of maximal rank returns [[neworder], U] where neworder is a reduced order and U the unimodular transformation matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnflllgram(GEN nf, GEN pol, GEN order, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfnormgroup: norm group computation with unchecked assumptions
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfnormgroup(bnr, pol) computes the norm (Artin/Takagi) group corresponding to Abelian extension defined by pol, assuming module of bnr is a multiple of conductor and pol defines Abelian extension. Result is HNF for norm group on given generators; if assumptions are false, function may return empty matrix or a wrong result (it does not check the assumptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfnormgroup(GEN bnr, GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolred: obsolete; prefer rnfpolredbest
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfpolred(nf, pol) is obsolete; use rnfpolredbest. It finds relative polynomials defining some subfields, but is slower/less efficient than rnfpolredbest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on incomplete lattice reduction theory (rnflllgram) and less recommended. Library syntax GEN rnfpolred(GEN nf, GEN pol, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolredabs: flags and complexity warnings
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfpolredabs(nf, pol, {flag = 0}) (obsolete: use rnfpolredbest) finds a simpler relative polynomial defining same field. Binary digits of flag mean: 1 - add information to convert elements to new representation; 2 - return absolute polynomial instead of relative; 16 - possibly use suborder of maximal order. Detailed mapping: 0 default return P; 1 returns [P,a]; 2 returns Pabs; 3 returns [Pabs,a,b]; 16 may be slower or faster depending on relative discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: complexity is exponential in absolute degree; rnfpolredbest runs in polynomial time and tends to return polynomials with smaller discriminants. Library syntax GEN rnfpolredabs(GEN nf, GEN pol, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpolredbest: relative polynomial reduction and flags
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfpolredbest(nf, pol, {flag = 0}) (relative version of polredbest) finds a simpler relative polynomial P defining same field and runs in polynomial time (not necessarily canonical minimal polynomial). Binary digits of flag: 1 - return [P,a]; 2 - return Pabs; 3 - return [Pabs, a, b].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show usage and returned P, a, b for conversions and substitution checks. Library syntax GEN rnfpolredbest(GEN nf, GEN pol, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfpseudobasis: outputs and meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfpseudobasis(nf, pol) computes a pseudo-basis (A, I) for maximal order ZL viewed as ZK-module and the relative discriminant, output as [A, I, D, d] where D is relative ideal discriminant and d is discriminant as element of nf*/nf*2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfpseudobasis(GEN nf, GEN pol).

rubrics_metrics.name: rnfsteinitz: steinitz class pseudo-basis
rubrics_metrics.description: rnfsteinitz(nf, x) given nf and polynomial or pseudo-basis x computes a pseudo-basis (A,I) such that all ideals of I except perhaps the last equal ring of integers of nf; outputs [A,I,D,d] as in rnfpseudobasis. The ideal class of last ideal of I is the Steinitz class of ZL as ZK-module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax GEN rnfsteinitz(GEN nf, GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: subgrouplist: subgroup enumeration and bounding
rubrics_metrics.description: subgrouplist(bnr, {bound}, {flag = 0}) outputs list of subgroups of finite Abelian group G (or bnr). Subgroups are given as HNF left divisors of SNF matrix corresponding to G. If flag=0 (default) and bnr from bnrinit, gives only subgroups whose modulus is the conductor; otherwise modulus ignored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If bound present and positive integer restrict output to subgroups of index < bound; if bound is vector [B] return subgroups of index exactly B. Examples include enumerating subfields of Q(zeta_n). Library syntax GEN subgrouplist0(GEN bnr, GEN bound = NULL, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: associative algebra basics: Jacobson radical and semisimplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: An algebra A has Jacobson radical = two-sided ideal of elements annihilating every simple left A-module. A is semisimple if Jacobson radical is trivial; semisimple algebra is isomorphic to direct sum of simple algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions guide decomposition and representation choices for algorithms manipulating associative algebras. No direct function; conceptual guidance at section start.

rubrics_metrics.name: central simple algebra degree and index
rubrics_metrics.description: For central simple algebra A over K, dimension is square d^2; integer d is called degree. A is isomorphic to M_d(D) for some central division algebra D of degree e; integer e is called index.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding degree/index is required when representing/constructing central simple algebras and choosing representations (matrix vs cyclic).

rubrics_metrics.name: cyclic algebra representation and natural order
rubrics_metrics.description: Given cyclic extension L/K degree d, generator σ and b∈K*, the cyclic algebra (L/K,σ,b) has basis ⊕_{i=0}^{d-1} x^i L with x^d=b and x·ℓ = σ(ℓ)·x for ℓ∈L; for integral b, the submodule O = ⊕_{i=0}^{d-1} x^i Z_L is an order called the natural order. Natural basis for O described in terms of Z-basis of ZL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating orders in central simple algebras, use natural order definitions; appropriate bases and normalization factors given for implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: natural order for central simple algebra via multiplication table
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is central simple algebra degree d over number field K with integral left multiplication table on basis (e_i) then O = ⊕_{i} Z_K e_i is natural order; the natural basis of O is b_j = ω_{j mod n} e_{floor(j/n)} / n where ω_i a Z-basis of Z_K (description as given).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides guidance for constructing integral orders from multiplication table representations.
